{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My grandmother knits me a sweater every Christmas. They're scratchy, unflattering, and I'm allergic to wool. For fifteen years I've worn each one during our holiday video calls, then donated them. She watches for me to wear them. I itch through every conversation.

CANDIDATE A:
My grandmother knits me a sweater every Christmas. Last year I finally told her gently that wool makes me itch. She was disappointed but appreciated my honesty. Now she knits me cotton scarves instead. Being truthful improved our gift-giving tradition.

CANDIDATE B:
My business partner's daughter painted a mural for our office. It's garish and clashes with our brand. For eight years I've scheduled client meetings around it, adjusting lighting to minimize its visibility while praising it to his face. He beams every time he shows it to visitors.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:25"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve enduring an uncomfortable situation to maintain another person's happiness, without revealing the true feelings about the situation."}
